thesis: This episode argues that Microsoft was a great business but a poor investment during the early 2000s due to high valuation, resulting in flat stock performance for over a decade before eventually delivering a 3x return. It also notes that Cisco was one of the three most valuable businesses on the planet in the early 2000s with a market cap over 600 billion.

claims.claim: The speaker views Microsoft as a great business but a bad investment due to high valuation in the early 2000s, though it eventually delivered a 3x return over 21 years.
claims.quote: And I told these Microsoft employees that men, that it looked like a bad investment to me. I said, it's a great business, but a bad investment.

claims.claim: Microsoft stock was flat with zero returns for 13-14 years from 2000 to 2012/2013 despite revenue and profit growth, making it a roller coaster ride.
claims.quote: But from 2000 till about 2012 or 2013, the stock was flat. Zero returns for 13, 14 years. Even though revenues had increased dramatically, profits had increased dramatically, because it was just so heavily overvalued.

claims.claim: If you had stayed with Microsoft from 2000 and somehow you were able to stomach the ride, you would have about more than three times starting capital, even from an elevated level.
claims.quote: So if you had, you know, stayed with Microsoft from 2000 and somehow you were able to stomach the ride, you know, it's not a, it's not a great outcome, but you have about more than three times starting capital, even from an elevated level.

claims.claim: Cisco was one of the three most valuable businesses on the planet in early 2000, with a market cap over 600 billion.
claims.quote: There were three companies in the world in early 2000, which had a market cap of over 600 billion, Microsoft, GE, and Cisco.
